problem: The caption says "only the CPU is shown as synthesizable RTL". Students can read this as saying the UART soft IP is not synthesizable RTL, which contradicts Section 1, where soft IP is defined as synthesizable RTL. The diagram simply does not print the RTL note under the UART box.
fix: Say: "Only the CPU node carries the 'synthesizable RTL' note; the UART is also soft IP, delivered as synthesizable RTL, and is drawn this way only to keep the figure short."

problem: "Every core needs an address in the memory map" is too strong. Blocks such as a PLL, a SerDes lane or a purely streaming datapath may have no memory-mapped registers, and a hard memory macro is addressed as memory, not as a core register space.
fix: Say: "Every core with a register interface needs a base address, size and access type in the memory map; blocks with no bus register interface, such as a PLL, are configured by dedicated signals instead."
